answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to bonded collateral and links correlated equivocation through shared evidence. When k coordinated identities equivocate, pairwise fault penalties scale as O(k²); detection also applies an exponential multiplier to capital loss across linked escrows, making a swarm costlier than isolated identities. Asymmetric depreciation prevents recovery from erasing the penalty. The ferrous reef is no fable: splitting one operator among aliases does not split its risk.
